extracted.intended_audience: graduate students and researchers in string theory / mathematical physics working on BRST cohomology and the NSR/Ramond sectors
extracted.subtask_description: Tools, definitions, and vanishing / no-ghost theorems for the BRST cohomology of Neveu–Schwarz and Ramond sectors of the NSR string, using filtrations, spectral sequences, double complexes, and constructions of inner products. Includes technical appendices proving cohomology computations and existence of positive-definite inner products.

rubrics_metrics.name: Filtration degree and filtration definition (VII.1.7–VII.1.8)
rubrics_metrics.description: Define the filtration degree fdeg of basis monomials (explicit formula given in (VII.1.7) and variants) and the (half-)integral filtration of C^∞ by F_p C^∞ = { ω ∈ C^∞ | fdeg ω ≥ p }.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The text emphasizes the explicit formula for fdeg (reads off contributions from each oscillator) and notes properties: F_p C^∞ ⊇ F_{p+1/2} C^∞ and the filtration is bounded. This filtration is the starting structure for constructing spectral sequences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Q preserves the filtration (filtered complex condition)
rubrics_metrics.description: Requirement Q F_p C^∞ ⊆ F_p C^∞; check the filtration-degree of each homogeneous term in Q to ensure non-negative filtration degrees.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The text lists filtration degrees of the oscillators and verifies that all terms of Q have non-negative filtration degree (with specified exceptions having positive degrees), hence Q preserves the filtration and {F_p C^∞} defines a bounded filtered complex.

rubrics_metrics.name: Existence of spectral sequence converging to H^∞ (Theorem II.1.32 usage)
rubrics_metrics.description: Given the bounded filtered complex, there exists a spectral sequence converging finitely to H^∞(N,V_0;M) whose E_1 term is the cohomology of the associated graded complex Gr C^∞ = ⊕_p Gr_p C^∞, and the differential on Gr is the part of Q of zero filtration degree.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The differential on the associated graded complex is precisely the zero-filtration-degree part of Q; terms with positive filtration degree drop out in Gr. This observation is used to identify the E_1 complex concretely.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identification of the graded differential and CL0 (VII.1.9–VII.1.10)
rubrics_metrics.description: On the associated graded complex, the induced differential can be identified with the differential on the complex C L_0 = C(N_+) ⊗ C^∞(N_-;M) & L_0, with explicit separation of ghosts and antighosts (the subspace with c ghosts and b antighosts is (CL_0)_{b,c} = C c(N_+) ⊗ C b^∞(N_-;M) & L_0).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This concrete identification makes it easy to keep track of ghost/antighost contributions and to compute the E_1 cohomology using Lie-superalgebra cochains for N_+ and cohomology of N_- with coefficients.

rubrics_metrics.name: Isomorphism H(CL0) ≅ H(C)_{L0} (VII.1.11–VII.1.15)
rubrics_metrics.description: C decomposes as C = C L_0 ⊕ L_0(C) and since L_0 commutes with Q, one shows H(C)_{L_0} (the L_0-invariant part of H(C)) is isomorphic to H(C L_0).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proof strategy: show inclusion H(C L_0) ⊆ H(C)_{L_0} by choosing L_0-invariant representatives, and the reverse inclusion by checking that if a class is L_0-invariant then it has an L_0-invariant representative. This permits computing cohomology on the smaller invariant subcomplex.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application of Künneth formula and E_1 computation (VII.1.16–VII.1.17)
rubrics_metrics.description: Use the Künneth formula H(C) ≅ H(N_+) ⊗ H^∞(N_-;M) to get the E_1 term Eb,c^1 = * H^c(N_+) ⊗ H_b^∞(N_-;M) + L_0; with Appendix A proving H_b^∞(N_-;M)=0 for b ≠ 0 and H_0^∞(N_-;M) ≅ C.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Combining these results yields that E_m^1 = 0 for m < 0 and therefore by spectral sequence convergence H_m^∞(N,V_0;M) = 0 for m < 0 (vanishing theorem for negative ghost number). Tracking ghosts and antighosts separately is important.

rubrics_metrics.name: Vanishing theorem and pairing by inner product (VII.1.18–VII.1.19)
rubrics_metrics.description: With a positive-definite inner product on H (Appendix C) and finite-dimensional Q-stable subspaces, one deduces H_m^∞(N,V_0;H) ≅ H_{-m}^∞(N,V_0;H), yielding the vanishing theorem H_{m^- = 0}^∞(N,V_0;H) = 0 (relative subcomplex vanishing).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The existence of a positive-definite inner product is essential to relate positive and negative ghost-number cohomology; this is used to propagate the vanishing results to paired degrees.

rubrics_metrics.name: Choice of representation for β_0, γ_0 zero-modes matters (Ramond sector)
rubrics_metrics.description: Two natural choices: Schrödinger representation (β_0 anti-hermitian, γ_0 hermitian on L^2(R)) where β_0 has no eigenvalues (so β_0 ω = 0 cannot be imposed), and Henneaux representation treating γ_0, β_0 as creation/annihilation operators with H ≅ C[γ_0].
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Changing hermiticity (treating β_0,γ_0 as creation/annihilation) can make Q non-hermitian, so cohomology may not inherit a well-defined inner product; conversely keeping original hermiticity destroys ghost-number grading. Both choices are studied: one yields graded vanishing theorems, the other yields inner-product structure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Relative subcomplex in Ramond Henneaux representation (VII.2.5–VII.2.9)
rubrics_metrics.description: Define C^∞(R,R_0;M) = { ω ∈ C^∞(R;M) | F_0 ω = b_0 ω = β_0 ω = 0 } (finite-dimensional). Filtration degree is defined (VII.2.8), filtration bounded, and a spectral sequence converges to H^∞(R,R_0;M) with E_1 term the differential for CF_0 = C(R_+) ⊗ C^∞(R_-;M) & F_0.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Although F_0 does not act reducibly, F_0 is nilpotent and one constructs an auxiliary double complex to compute cohomology; vertical cohomology reduces to CF_0 in degree zero because HF_0 is trivial under stated conditions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Construction of double complex K_{p,q} for F_0 cochains (VII.2.10–VII.2.15)
rubrics_metrics.description: Define K_{p,q} = C^q(F_0; (C_p)_{L_0}), with horizontal differential d (extension of Q) and vertical coboundary δ for F_0; total differential D = d + δ computes the total cohomology K = ⊕_m K_m.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because C L_0 is finite-dimensional and graded by ghost number, use spectral sequences (vertical then horizontal filtrations) to show vertical cohomology vanishes except in q=0 (isomorphic to C F_0), and therefore total cohomology is H(C F_0). This is the key step to prove vanishing theorems in the Ramond sector.

rubrics_metrics.name: Vanishing of HF_0 and collapse of spectral sequence (VII.2.13–VII.2.17)
rubrics_metrics.description: The cohomology H_{F_0}((C_p)_{L_0}) is trivial (except q=0), therefore the spectral sequence collapses and gives H_m(CF_0) = 0 for m < 0 and hence H^∞(R,R_0;M) = 0 for m < 0; similarly for full Fock space H^∞(R,R_0;H) and relative vanishing statements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A technical argument (choice of q and F_0(q) etc.) proves HF_0 triviality except for degenerate vacuum states; this triviality is essential to conclude the vanishing theorem for the Ramond relative cohomology.

rubrics_metrics.name: Schrödinger representation decomposition and isomorphism HQ(CF_0) ≅ H^∞(R,V_0;M) (VII.2.18–VII.2.27)
rubrics_metrics.description: Represent β_0, γ_0 in terms of a, a† and decompose the relative subcomplex as C ⊗ C[a†]; the differential becomes Q = Q ⊗ 1 + 1/√2 (F_0 + K) ⊗ a† + 1/√2 (F_0 − K) ⊗ a, with relations F_0^2 = 0, Q^2 = F_0 K. The cohomology of F_0 + K is isomorphic to that of F_0 (via conjugation by exp(T)), and one proves HQ(CF_0) ≅ H^∞(R,V_0;M).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proof uses polynomial expansion in a† and the vanishing of cohomology of F_0 + K to reduce cocycles to constant terms; exp(±T) gives an isomorphism of cohomologies. Consequence: in Schrödinger representation the cohomology is only an ungraded vector space (ghost-number operator on C[a†] has no eigenvalues).

rubrics_metrics.name: Isomorphism between relative and full cohomology and spectral-sequence argument for full complex (VII.3.1–VII.3.3)
rubrics_metrics.description: One shows H^∞(R,V_0;H) ≅ H^∞(R,R_0;H) and more generally H_n^∞(N;H) ≅/= H_0^∞(N,V_0;H) for n = ±1/2 otherwise (and similar for Ramond), using a Koszul-type spectral-sequence or double-complex argument whose E_2 term is H^∞(R,V_0;H) ⊗ H(V_0).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because V_0 acts diagonally in the relative subcomplex and H^n(V_0) is known (nonzero only for n = ±1/2), the spectral sequence collapses at E_2 by vanishing in relative cohomology and yields explicit possible nonzero degrees in the full cohomology.

rubrics_metrics.name: No-ghost theorem via equality of character and signature (VII.4.1–VII.4.5 and following)
rubrics_metrics.description: Prove ch_q H^∞ = Tr_{C^∞} q^L and sgn_q H^∞ = Tr_{C^∞} q^L (-1)^{N_gh}, compute traces factor-by-factor over oscillator Hilbert spaces and show the two generating functions agree, establishing the no-ghost theorem for Neveu–Schwarz and Ramond sectors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compute contributions from {a}, {b,c} oscillators and from superghost sectors (separately for NS and R), using multiplicativity of trace over tensor products. Matching character and signature (same q-series) implies positive-definiteness of cohomology inner product (no ghosts).

rubrics_metrics.name: Appendix A: cohomology of S_- with free module coefficients (Theorem VII.A.1)
rubrics_metrics.description: Let M ≅ U(S_-) be a free S_--module. Then H_m^∞(S_-;M) ≅ C for b = 0 and 0 otherwise (equation VII.A.2).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proof: decompose S_- into even and odd parts, construct bases for cochains, define filtration degree fdeg = K+L+M+N, compute graded differential d which has an explicit zero-filtration-degree part, define an operator Γ with (d Γ + Γ d)Ω = (K+L+M+N) Ω so that positive-degree cohomology vanishes; long exact sequence yields final result.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appendix B: every cohomology class has a singlet (T-annihilated) representative
rubrics_metrics.description: Using the sl(2,C) algebra generated by T, T^*, and N_gh (with commutation relations (VII.B.1)) and Weyl's theorem on complete reducibility on finite-dimensional L,P_μ eigenspaces, every BRST cohomology class in H^0_Q(CF_0) has a representative cocycle annihilated by T (an sl(2,C)-invariant).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Construct the needed representative by solving T ξ = −ρ (mod ker Q) where ρ = G Q^* T ψ and using ξ = −(T^* T)^{-1} T^* ρ inside the image of T^* (inverse exists on that subspace). The projection operator given yields the singlet representative explicitly (equation VII.B.3). Singlet representatives are not necessarily unique.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appendix C: construction of a positive-definite inner product via an involution C
rubrics_metrics.description: Define a self-adjoint involution C acting on the Fock space so that the new inner product <ψ, φ>_C = (ψ, C φ) is positive-definite (where ( , ) is the original inner product); explicit action of C is given on the various oscillators and zero-modes (formulas VII.C.2–VII.C.10).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: On ghosts/antighost oscillators C plays the role of the Serre–Hodge operator; conventions for mode expansions are fixed. For the β_0, γ_0 zero-modes two choices arise: either self-adjoint (positive-definite inner product immediate) or treat them as creation/annihilation operators (then no global involution C exists but adjoints can be defined within that representation). Verifying positivity of the resulting inner product is left to the reader.
